notes.tier: the reason for the tier set in the top-level "tier" field (1, 2, or 3)
notes.minimums: each countable minimum, pass or fail
notes.persona_answers: your answers to the two persona questions
notes.keyword_mirror: posting term | your term | where on the page; swaps you approved
notes.contact: who you reached out to before applying, or none found
notes.bridge_source: which bank card the bridge sentence rests on, and the posting words it mirrors

posting_map.ask: <the posting's first and most emphasized theme, in its words, short>
posting_map.answer: <group label on the page, or 'letter pN', or 'honest gap'>

notes._posting_map_rule: 3 to 5 themes in the posting's own order of emphasis; the group order on the page follows it; the first group carries your strongest unique-match story and answers one of the top two themes; labels in your words, never the posting's heading verbatim; a required theme with no evidence is an honest gap, not a thin group.
notes.tools: leave "tools" as "A.tools" for the whole line, or write {"text": "a subset of your A.tools line"}
notes.credentials: delete the "credentials" key if you have none, so no Credentials heading prints

letter_sources._rule: One entry per body paragraph of the cover letter, in order: the bank card ID(s) it rests on, or your dated statement in your words (session date). The gate flags a letter whose selection file lists fewer sources than the letter has paragraphs. A paragraph with no source is cut, not softened.

profile.bridge: One sentence in the posting's words, resting on a named bank card. Delete the bridge key to use the profile as is.

timeline._rule: Claude keeps the clock: timestamps for drafting_started, vN_delivered for every version, correction_vN for each correction message, and submitted. At 'submitted', compute hours spent and cycle time and write both to the tracker.
